note: Mount Washington Valley local desk: Conway (including North Conway), Bartlett, Jackson and Madison. North Conway is a village inside the Town of Conway. Police, roads, the transfer station and elections are run by the Town of Conway; fire protection, water and sewer in North Conway come from the North Conway Water Precinct. Checked Oct 30, 2026 from town, precinct and department pages and local news. Every item links to its source.

region.source: Redfin, Carroll County NH housing market
region.summary: Carroll County, three months ending July 2026 (Redfin): median sale price $498,538, up 6.1% from a year earlier. 116 homes sold in July, up from 110. Homes sold after 52 days on the market, compared with 51 a year earlier. For single-family homes only, North Conway Realty counted 156 county sales in the first quarter of 2026 (155 a year earlier), with an average price of $659,578 and 87 days on market, up from 62.

mount-washington-valley.note: Redfin's Conway page, the only local page with full market figures; Redfin does not say whether it covers the whole town or just Conway Village. Homes sold is August only. Redfin rates the market somewhat competitive (47 of 100) with a 97.6% sale-to-list ratio. Redfin's separate North Conway page shows only a one-month median of $646,000, up 39.0% from a year earlier, with no sales count.

election.absentee: Absentee voting is for voters who will be out of town on Election Day, have a disability or illness that keeps them from voting in person, or have work or caregiving duties. burnPermits.text: New Hampshire requires a written permit for outdoor burning unless the ground is covered with snow. Get one from the local Forest Fire Warden or fire department, or online at NHFirePermit.com if the town takes part. You must be 18 or older.

benchmarks.note: FBI figures for 2024, the latest year with matching town, state and national numbers. Rates are offenses reported to police per 100,000 residents; Conway's figures cover the whole town (population 10,441), including North Conway. Conway draws large numbers of visitors and shoppers who aren't counted as residents, which pushes per-resident rates up. The FBI advises against ranking places on these numbers alone.

valleyDepartments.nonEmergency: 603-383-9292 (listed as contact number, not labeled non-emergency)
valleyDepartments.note: The Highway Department page lists the Carroll County Sheriff's Office, 800-552-8960, for emergencies besides 911. The police page gives no street address.

valleyDepartments.name: Jackson Fire Department
valleyDepartments.note: The page gives only the Town Offices mailing address (54 Main Street, PO Box 268). Fire permits are linked from the department page.

valleyDepartments.name: Town of Madison Police Department
valleyDepartments.address: 1923 Village Road (Town Hall, lower level), Madison, NH 03849
valleyDepartments.note: The page posts monthly calls-for-service logs; the latest listed are August to November 2025.

valleyDepartments.name: Town of Madison Fire/Rescue
valleyDepartments.chief: Michael Brooks (Fire Chief and Fire Warden)
valleyDepartments.note: A volunteer department. Fire permits are required for all outdoor burning; notify Carroll County Dispatch (603-539-2263) before burning.

valleyDepartments.name: Bartlett/Jackson Ambulance
valleyDepartments.detail: Linked from the Jackson town site; not opened.

valleyDepartments.name: Ossipee Police Department
valleyDepartments.chief: James Sullivan (interim from May 2026; named chief June 5, 2026)
valleyDepartments.note: Phone and address were not found in an opened source (the town website could not be read). At the March 2026 Town Meeting voters passed a non-binding article asking the department to end its 287(g) agreement with ICE, 75-56.

valleyDepartments.name: Center Ossipee Fire & Rescue Department
valleyDepartments.chief: Dana Cullen Jr. (2023 town report; not confirmed for 2026)
valleyDepartments.note: Run by the Center Ossipee fire precinct, a separate local district. Reported 506 emergency runs in 2023. In January 2026 the Selectmen approved its agreement with Action Ambulance.

valleyDepartments.name: Ossipee Corner Fire Department
valleyDepartments.chief: Adam Riley (2023 town report; not confirmed for 2026)
valleyDepartments.note: Run by the Ossipee Corner fire precinct. Reported 503 emergency calls in 2023. Riley was also the town's Forest Fire Warden; fire permits come from the fire departments.

valleyDepartments.name: West Ossipee Fire Department
valleyDepartments.chief: Carl Huddleston (2023 town report; not confirmed for 2026)
valleyDepartments.note: Run by the West Ossipee fire precinct, a separate local district.

valleyDepartments.name: Action Ambulance (town contract)
valleyDepartments.detail: Ossipee has a town-wide ambulance contract with Action Ambulance; the 2026 budget review listed an ambulance contract line of $464,423 (AI summary of a December 2025 Budget Committee meeting).

valleyDepartments.name: Tamworth Police Department
valleyDepartments.nonEmergency: 603-323-8581 (department line; the page says to call it to reach an on-duty officer, including Animal Control)
valleyDepartments.address: 100 Tamworth Road (Route 113), P.O. Box 69, Tamworth, NH 03886
valleyDepartments.note: Dispatch is through the Carroll County Sheriff's Office, 603-539-2284. The page links yearly police statistics pages for 2021 to 2026; no daily logs are posted.

valleyDepartments.name: Tamworth Fire Rescue Department
valleyDepartments.chief: Richard Colcord (Fire Chief and Forest Fire Warden; Jim Bowles and Matt Baumann, assistant chiefs)
valleyDepartments.note: Overseen by a five-member Board of Firewards. The department provides fire protection and emergency medical services; its page does not say who provides ambulance transport, though the town budget has a separate Ambulance line ($236,814 in the 2026 draft). The 2024 annual report also refers to Chocorua, Wonalancet and South Tamworth fire stations. Fire permits through nh.burnsafeamerica.com. Dispatch: Carroll County Sheriff's Office, 603-539-2284.

notHere.title: Route 16 and other state roads
notHere.text: Route 16 (White Mountain Highway and Main Street) and Routes 113 and 153 are state highways. Projects on them, like the Conway Village Main Street rebuild, are NH Department of Transportation work; the town engineer posts updates.
notHere.label: NHDOT project notice

notHere.title: Schools
notHere.text: Conway's public schools, including Kennett High School, are run through SAU 9 and the school district, which votes on its own ballot, not by the town.
notHere.label: SAU 9

notHere.title: Fire, water and sewer in North Conway
notHere.text: The North Conway Water Precinct, not the town, runs the North Conway Fire Department and North Conway's water and sewer systems. Water: 603-356-5382.
notHere.label: precinct departments
